title: New Keyboard manager not work "KANA" emulation.

status.label: Confirm KANA remapping with the current Japanese IME
status.detail: The report gives a specific new-editor mapping and Japanese Windows environment, but no current-version confirmation or native IME comparison.

judgment.rationale: The reporter describes a precise new-editor mapping from Ctrl+Caps Lock to Ctrl+Shift+KANA on Windows 11 25H2 Japanese and says it does not toggle Roman/KANA input mode. The report includes diagnostics but no comments or current-version confirmation. The active IME and whether Windows recognizes the emitted KANA sequence outside Keyboard Manager are needed to distinguish an IME expectation change from an event-injection defect.
evidence: The issue lists PowerToys 0.98.0 on Windows 11 25H2 Pro Japanese.
The trigger is Ctrl+Caps Lock shown as VK240, and the action is Ctrl+Shift+KANA in the new Keyboard Manager editor.
The reporter expects Roman/KANA input-mode toggling and says the mapping does not work.
The reporter notes the older Ctrl+Caps Lock toggle is no longer supported and attached a PowerToys diagnostic ZIP.
The issue is open and unassigned; no linked fix or follow-up was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for current-version behavior, the active Japanese IME, and whether the same KANA sequence changes input mode outside this mapping; use the existing diagnostics rather than asking for a duplicate upload.

fix_assessment.rationale: If the current Japanese IME accepts the same KANA sequence outside Keyboard Manager but not through the new editor mapping, the remapping pipeline may mishandle the IME-specific event. Native IME behavior and current-version persistence are not yet established.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve IME KANA key events in new Keyboard Manager mappings
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The new editor's capture or output pipeline may not preserve the KANA virtual-key event and modifier combination required by the active Japanese IME. It is also possible the IME no longer handles that sequence; an outside-Keyboard-Manager comparison is needed.
plan: Confirm the failure on current stable with the exact trigger and action in the report.
Compare the same Ctrl+Shift+KANA sequence outside the mapping using the same IME.
Trace capture, persistence, and emission of the VK240/KANA event and modifiers in the new editor.
If the pipeline mishandles a supported IME event, correct it and add a focused Japanese-IME regression test.
verification: Verify the configured trigger toggles the active IME between Roman and KANA modes on current stable.
Verify the same input sequence behaves consistently when emitted outside and through Keyboard Manager.
Confirm the new editor retains the KANA key and modifier configuration after saving and reopening.

confidence.rationale: The mapping and environment are precisely described, but native IME handling and current-version behavior have not been confirmed.

known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.98.0, Windows 11 25H2 Pro Japanese, and the new Keyboard Manager editor.
The trigger is Ctrl+Caps Lock shown as VK240; the action is Ctrl+Shift+KANA.
The reporter says the mapping does not toggle input mode and notes that the older Ctrl+Caps Lock toggle is no longer supported.
A PowerToys diagnostic ZIP is already attached; there are no comments or current-version confirmation.
inferences: The failure may involve how the new editor captures or emits an IME-specific KANA event, but the report does not show whether the active IME accepts the same sequence outside Keyboard Manager.
issue_context.analysis: The exact mapping is suitable for reproduction. Confirm current-version behavior and the active IME's response to the same sequence before assuming that PowerToys should restore the legacy Ctrl+Caps Lock behavior.
initial_investigation: Read the issue body, exact mapping, environment, labels, state, and existing diagnostic attachment.
No linked fix, comments, or cross-reference was found.

information_gaps.information: Whether the mapping still fails on current stable, the active Japanese IME, and whether Ctrl+Shift+KANA toggles input mode when generated outside Keyboard Manager
information_gaps.why_needed: This separates a Keyboard Manager event-capture/emission failure from an IME or Windows behavior change, including the reported loss of the legacy Ctrl+Caps Lock toggle.

Could you confirm whether it still fails on current stable, name the active Japanese IME, and say whether the same Ctrl+Shift+KANA sequence toggles Roman/KANA mode outside this Keyboard Manager mapping (for example with a physical KANA key if available)? reproduce.title: Verify KANA key remapping in Japanese Windows
setup: Create a trigger of Ctrl+Caps Lock (VK240) and map it to Ctrl+Shift+KANA.
steps: Save the mapping and reopen the editor to confirm the trigger and action are retained.
Invoke the trigger and observe whether the active IME changes between Roman and KANA input modes.
